metadata_scope.legacy_adult_routing: AT01-AT04 are maintained legacy fallback recipes. Current new adult app requests for non-running catalog goals use program-catalog.ts; existing saved legacy targets can still be reviewed.
metadata_scope.unresolved_aliases: The SC/AR source and rule aliases are inherited metadata with no resolving registry in this repository. They are preserved historical metadata, not independently verified citations or executable rule IDs. Runtime evidence uses the reviewed IDs in program-evidence.ts.
metadata_scope.youth_policy_runtime_difference: The detailed youth policy below is not executed by the current generator. YOUTH-FOUNDATION uses one set of eight reps initially, then staggered second sets after two comfortable supervised prerequisite sessions; youth load and rep changes remain supervisor-owned.
metadata_scope.exact_template_validation: Published principles inform these app defaults; no independent validation or individual optimality of these exact templates is claimed.

adult.name: Adult foundation and general fitness
adult.eligible: Healthy adult beginner, or a person choosing a modest resistance-training base; apply return modifier when appropriate.
adult.numeric_status: Published ranges inform the template; exact six-week layout, selected exercises, and repetition schedule are prototype defaults.

slots.example: Light dumbbell Romanian deadlift or hip bridge
Machine chest press or elevated push-up
Same selected squat or leg press
Same selected press or elevated push-up
Same selected seated dumbbell or machine press

accepted_block_example.week_1: One working set per slot, target lower end of range, familiarization effort.
accepted_block_example.week_2: Use the listed sets; keep lower-end repetition target.
accepted_block_example.weeks_3_to_6: Accepted target for 8–12 slots advances to 9, 10, 11, then 12 at the confirmed working load. Calf and trunk targets may remain fixed until reviewed.
accepted_block_example.important: The calendar does not establish readiness. If feedback conflicts with the scheduled increase, display a hold/reduction proposal before the affected exercise. Do not require all repetitions or punish a smaller completed training amount.

adult.minimum_time_variant: If the user's actual available time is insufficient, propose a shorter full-body session with one set per main slot and retained rest; display the resulting training amount before acceptance.

adult.name: Adult hypertrophy and bodybuilding foundation
adult.eligible: Healthy adult with consistent lifting experience who can accommodate four sessions and tolerate the selected volume; beginners enter through AT01.
adult.numeric_status: The split, exercises, set distribution, rest timers, and block length are prototype defaults. The general higher-volume direction is supported.

sessions.modification: Swap which confirmed chest and back exercise receives the first 3-set slot; retain the same selected variants. The two later chest/back slots each receive 2 sets.
Keep the same training amount; use a confirmed leg-press or squat alternative for the first slot if variety was selected in the accepted plan.

adult.accounting_limit: This role-based accounting is a transparent planning convention. Presses and pulls also load arms/shoulders; secondary involvement is displayed separately. Do not invent validated fractional set credits or claim every muscle gets the same biological training amount.
adult.accepted_block_example: Keep weekly set counts stable. For 8–12 slots, schedule 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 12 across weeks 1–6 at confirmed loads; for 10–15 slots schedule 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. New feedback-driven load or set changes require a proposal. The sixth week is review, not an obligatory deload.
adult.time_or_recovery_constraint: Offer lower set counts or AT01/AT03 before acceptance when time or history does not support this training amount; do not declare fewer than ten sets ineffective.

adult.name: Adult strength with optional powerbuilding emphasis
adult.eligible: Healthy adult with stable experience in the selected main lifts; competition-lift versions require familiarity with those lifts and appropriate equipment.
adult.numeric_status: Specific main-lift frequency, accessories, six-week progression, and hybrid balance are prototype defaults; no independently validated powerbuilding protocol is claimed.
adult.main_load: For experienced main-lift work, a supported recent 1RM can inform approximately 80% as an initial reference; actual capacity, selected repetitions, equipment, and the 2–3 RIR target take precedence. Without a supported maximum, use recent comparable sets instead of claiming a precise percentage.
adult.accepted_block_example: Main 3–5 slots use 3, 4, 5, 3, 4, 5 repetitions by week. Weeks 4–6 may use a small precomputed available increment only if that actual load was shown and accepted initially; otherwise keep the confirmed load and propose any increase. Secondary 5–8 slots use 5, 6, 7, 8, 8, 8.
adult.powerbuilding_option: Add two 10–15-repetition sets of one chosen upper-body accessory on A and one chosen lower-body accessory on B, with 90-second rest, only when this fits the accepted time budget. Alternatively choose AT02 when hypertrophy is clearly primary. This option does not promise hypertrophy-optimal volume for every muscle.
adult.competition_stability: Preserve squat, bench, and deadlift competition variants if the goal is powerlifting. An alternative is tracked as an alternative; its results do not silently replace the competition lift's history. This is an ordinary training block, not a meet-peaking plan.
adult.rest_extension: Allow 3–5 minutes for demanding main work without lowering a completion score.

adult.name: Adult home resistance and basic calisthenics
adult.eligible: Healthy adult seeking scalable bodyweight/band training; excludes unsupported advanced skills and apparatus-dependent maneuvers.
adult.numeric_status: Full-body selection, exact training amount, six-week layout, and variant ladder are prototype defaults; SC06 directly supports only the studied push-up comparison.

sessions.modification: Repeat confirmed variants; a user-selected supported split squat may replace the squat with its own baseline.

adult.accepted_block_example: Week 1 has one working set per slot; week 2 uses listed sets. Rep targets then increase within each range in the accepted calendar. Keep the same assistance, support height, band, and setup until a variant-change proposal is accepted.
adult.progression: Advance repetitions first; then offer a measured support-height change, lower assistance, a different resistance band, or external load. Exact variant changes are selected options, not equivalent percentage-load increments.
adult.equipment_gap: If there is no suitable pulling equipment or anchor, show incomplete pulling coverage and propose an equipment-supported alternative. Do not improvise an unsafe household anchor or claim an unresisted movement supplies the same stimulus.

accepted_numeric_repetition_schedule.label: Prototype targets in the accepted six-week plan; feedback-driven deviations remain proposals.

youth.design_status: All choices below are prototype policy inside consensus envelopes, not trial-validated app rules.

eligibility.mode: app-directed general foundation or coach-agreed offseason foundation
required: User reports a qualified adult youth resistance-training supervisor will be present for this session.
Appropriate equipment and environment confirmed by the responsible adult.
No unresolved symptom/injury/illness restriction that prevents this planned activity.
Existing team, PE, club and other exercise commitments entered or explicitly marked unknown.
eligibility.external_supervision_definition: Qualified means relevant youth resistance-training knowledge and practical experience, not merely any adult or a parent account. An attestation is reported availability, not verification by the app.
eligibility.supervisor_unavailable: Allow educational content, plan preview and manual activity logging. Do not launch this guided loaded-youth template or generate load progressions. Show how to arrange qualified instruction. Do not mislabel videos as supervision.
eligibility.coached_in_season: Tracking mode by default; no app-added strength prescription. A coach-agreed complementary program requires an explicit authority switch and a reviewed total schedule.

schedule.block_length_basis: 8 weeks is a product planning horizon; no guarantee of adaptation or mandatory automatic advancement.
schedule.time_conflict: Shorten the exercise menu with review or offer a different confirmed slot; do not remove recovery or rush technique to fit.

exercise_selection.basis: Six simple slots cover lower body, upper push/pull and trunk; exact count and selections are product choices. The supervisor selects equipment, range and regression individually.
exercise_selection.order: Warm-up, movement instruction/practice, larger/simple multijoint patterns, other work, trunk, cooldown.

session_A.load: individually selected assistance or light resistance
practice without added load initially; no forced repetitions if still learning
incline or machine setting selected by supervisor; body weight is not assumed easy

alternatives: light goblet squat after external instruction
session_B.load: keep the chosen core movement stable
same familiar choice as A where practical

exclusions_from_default: unreviewed custom exercises for automated progression
exercise_selection.limitations: This is a general foundation, not a claim of an optimal football-quarterback, basketball-center or baseball-pitcher program. Familiarization can replace working sets rather than adding work.

starting_dose.familiarization: Instruction and individually chosen low/no-load practice before exercise becomes eligible for working-set progression. Complex movement practice may be 1–3 repetitions with external feedback; do not force 8–12 while learning.
starting_dose.rest_basis: 90 seconds is a conservative product timer, not an AAP exact target; user/supervisor may extend. Do not require starting the next set when not ready.
starting_dose.unilateral_reps: Display per side and log per side; no hidden doubling of prescribed count.
starting_dose.starting_load_label: Choose appropriate light resistance with your supervisor
starting_dose.load_calculation: No age-, sex-, body-weight- or position-based load guess; no novice e1RM computation. A standard empty bar can be excessive. Track band/setup/assistance explicitly.
starting_dose.effort: Comfortable controlled practice, without undue fatigue; do not chase failure. Optional RPE informs discussion and history but cannot certify load or technique.
starting_dose.percent_1RM_policy: Retain ≤60% as source metadata and professional context. Do not claim the user is below it without a credible assessment; no forced testing to populate it.

progression.eligibility_count_basis: Two comparable successful supervised exposures is an auditable product rule, not a validated biological threshold.
progression.comparable: Same exercise/version, equipment, units, assistance, rep definition and relevant load basis.
required_each_exposure: Planned working reps completed and actuals logged.
User reports supervisor found the selected exercise/load appropriate; the app makes no technique assessment.
No reported pain, illness or unresolved restrictions affecting the work.
No new schedule/recovery concern calling for a deviation.
No uncertainty requiring another familiarization exposure.
sequence: Keep one working set while establishing exercise familiarity.
After two eligible exposures at the current prescription, add one repetition per working set, up to 12.
Once one set of 12 is achieved on two eligible exposures, the disclosed plan may add a second set at 8 repetitions; change no external load that day.
Stagger new second sets: at most one exercise gains a set in a session, and only if session time and total sport load permit. This is product policy; do not apply to a crowded in-season week.
With two sets established, build repetitions toward 12 using the same two-exposure rule.
After two eligible exposures of two sets of 12, increase external resistance by the smallest practical increment no greater than 5%, then return to two sets of 8.
If no increment at or below 5% exists, keep the current load; do not round upward. Seek smaller equipment increments or a separately accepted revised variation.
Never add load and sets simultaneously. Never progress merely because a calendar week elapsed.
progression.load_cap_basis: Up to 5% is a conservative prototype ceiling at the low end of the published 5–10% recommendation; smaller increments are product choices, not a separate proven optimum.
progression.non_numeric_resistance: No percentage calculation for zero added load, body-weight assistance, bands or changed lever/ROM. A new progression variation needs external selection and a separate proposal, with a new baseline.
progression.progress_to_advanced: Do not silently move to heavier/advanced templates. Propose a separately accepted next block; carry history and supervision context.
progression.feedback_changes: Any feedback-based alteration outside the accepted conditional schedule is shown as a proposal with accept/decline. Day moves always require confirmation. A symptom-related hold must not continue to display an affirmative recommendation to push through.
